_meta.note: Seed data from manual research, July 2026. The research module should refresh this periodically by pulling from RoMonitor Stats / Rolimon's / Roblox charts, not hand-edit it forever.

top_games_snapshot.name: Grow a Garden
top_games_snapshot.why_it_works: Scarcity + trading economy, low barrier to entry, huge word-of-mouth spike

top_games_snapshot.name: Steal a Brainrot
top_games_snapshot.why_it_works: Rode a meme wave with simple mechanics, ~20 min to learn, outperformed much higher-budget games via cultural timing

top_games_snapshot.name: Brookhaven RP
top_games_snapshot.why_it_works: No objectives or tutorial, pure social hangout, sustained by Spatial Voice chat, long sessions (45+ min)

top_games_snapshot.name: Adopt Me!
top_games_snapshot.why_it_works: Player-to-player value generation via trading and pet economy, long-term LiveOps cadence

top_games_snapshot.name: Pet Simulator 99
top_games_snapshot.why_it_works: Scarcity + trading + event-based rewards extend player lifetime and revenue

top_games_snapshot.name: 99 Nights in the Forest
top_games_snapshot.why_it_works: Sustained dread over jump scares, real skill gap between players who learn systems vs. react blindly

top_games_snapshot.name: Blox Fruits
top_games_snapshot.why_it_works: Grew from a niche anime IP tie-in into a long-running progression RPG

top_games_snapshot.name: RIVALS
top_games_snapshot.why_it_works: Successfully captured competitive FPS players, historically a hard audience for Roblox to retain

brainrot_meme.growth_shape: fast spike, short tail unless mechanics get deepened post-launch
brainrot_meme.core_loop: simple, learnable in under 20 minutes, rides an existing meme/cultural reference
brainrot_meme.risk: high volume competition, easy to feel derivative, algorithm buries slow launches

simulator.growth_shape: slower build, long tail if economy is right
simulator.core_loop: collect -> upgrade -> unlock -> repeat, with scarcity and trading layered in
simulator.risk: needs real economy design (sinks/faucets) or inflation kills it in weeks

roleplay_social.growth_shape: slow build, very long tail, session length compounds over time
roleplay_social.core_loop: no strict objectives, social tools (voice, customization, hangout spaces) matter more than content volume
roleplay_social.risk: hardest to auto-generate meaningfully; social trust and community moderation matter a lot

horror_survival.growth_shape: spike on release if atmosphere lands, decent tail if systems have depth
horror_survival.core_loop: escalating difficulty/threat over a bounded run (e.g. survive N nights/days)
horror_survival.risk: jump-scare-only design flattens fast; needs a learnable system underneath the scares

cross_cutting_success_factors: Player-to-player value generation (trading, gifting, showing off) outperforms pure solo content volume
LiveOps cadence (regular events/updates) is treated as non-optional by top studios in 2026
Discovery algorithm rewards retention/session length far more than upload frequency
Games with genuine systems depth create a skill gap that keeps engaged players around longer
